title: AC1027 DataStorage zero/one/four/twelve-record explicit-anchor controls
scope: Extend the existing PAR-07/S8.3 DataStorage alignment control beyond four records
Exercise empty, single-record, four-record, and twelve-record indexes with explicit data anchors
Preserve local fast-test cadence and repository fixture restrictions

sections: 24.2.2.3 data file segment and record offsets
specification.summary: The segment header object-data alignment value is an offset in 16-byte units from the data segment start. Data-index local offsets identify record headers, and record data is found from the explicit data-start marker plus each record-local offset.

changes: Replaced the four-record-only test body with a shared in-memory profile builder for zero, one, four, and twelve data records.
Uses explicit object-data offsets of 64, 96, 192, and 320 bytes respectively, each beyond the count-derived aligned record-header end.
The twelve-record case expands the data-index segment, permutes index-row order independently of physical record order, assigns unique handles/payloads, and includes a trailing sentinel payload.
Checks segment anchor, structural validity, replay eligibility, record count, and exact handle-to-payload associations.
implementation.zeroRecordLimit: The zero-record case verifies an empty data-record index in a minimal generated section. It does not claim to recreate the complete default schema-only DataStorage section shown in ODA §24.3.
implementation.fixturePolicy: All DWG-section bytes are built in memory from scratch. No DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB fixture file was created or added.
